events.text: PO $320. Buy-side cal-26 EPS $13–15 vs sell-side ~$8.50; ~70% of the sector's economics on ~50%+ of the units. Rubin: the large customer ramp is Q4, not Q3. On the agentic CPU:GPU ratio — "pure BS".

Revenue $82B (+85% y/y), DC $75B (+92%). Guide Q2 $91B ±2%. $1T Blackwell+Rubin (cal25–27). Vera Rubin ships Q3. Vera CPU = $200B TAM / ~$20B this year. GM 75%. $80B buyback + dividend. China DC = $0 in the outlook.

The $20B of CPU is mostly systems/head-nodes + DRAM — "apples-to-apples" on the chip is ~$5B. GM 75% defensible even with HBM4E ~2x (consignment helps). Supply $119B → capacity for ~$130B of revenue exiting the year. DC has outpaced hyperscaler capex for 5 quarters.

NVDA remains a "funding short" — the thesis hasn't broken, but the buy-side sees larger inflections in other names. Rubin capacity ~2M units in Q4. Axion mix ~60% / Graviton ~60% higher than expected = headwind for x86.
NVDA still ~50%+ of TSMC's CoWoS allocation in 2027 — the packaging bottleneck remains favorable to NVDA.
Cloud DC capex +80% '26 / +50% '27 (~$575B). Agentic = 10–100x compute per user. Enterprise is NVDA's stronghold (~95% share). ASIC $70–75B at 40–50% CAGR.
Hold, PT $255 — on valuation. Nothing wrong with the fundamentals; the question is the multiple.

Kyber rack (2027/28) = the 800V DC inflection. Vera Rubin (mid-2027) still on the 480V shelf. NVDA targets ~7% of electrical efficiency gain — "so the customer buys more chips". Power $ content only accelerates in 2027+.

If forced to choose, prefers NVDA to AVGO: NVDA's multiple has already collapsed, AVGO "still has room to fall". GPU/ASIC split ~70/30 durable; NVDA gaining share at Anthropic; more degrees of freedom.
NVDA ~50%+ of CoWoS in 2027; total GPU production "could reach 10mn+ in 2027". Vera CPU migrates to ASE FoCoS packaging (outside the CoWoS queue).
GB300 NVL72 dominates all systems ($0.156/Mtok) — the 72-GPU NVLink domain wins. CUDA Day-0 (SGLang/vLLM), but NVDA's own TensorRT-LLM shipped with bugs. Warning: Huawei CANN now also delivers Day-0.
Jensen: "next year's 2H much bigger than this one"; memory scarcity should "persist for several years".
Low PE = market doubting the sustainability of demand. Oracle F27 capex/sales >100%; hyperscalers don't generate FCF; "picks-and-shovels making a fortune, but low PEs". "Toxic" price war.
Pokes at the cost economics of the GPU datacenter — questions the return on the capital deployed in the buildout.

"Over on earnings, under on the multiple" — nothing bad in the fundamentals, but a persistently low multiple. The Anthropic deal helps: it grows a model-builder that reinvests in capex. WFE $250B in 2028.
NVDA the "popular funding short", behind SOX/AMD; "hard to find a high-conviction upside catalyst" near term.
NVDA captures $25–35B of revenue/GW (~2x AMD). GPU units 6.2M→8.9M→9.9M. But ASIC share of units 42%(26E)→53%(27E) — ASIC overtakes merchant GPU in 2027; Broadcom AI $60B→$150B+.
Top Pick, OW PT $288. "Definitively the best product in the market"; best token-per-watt and AI-factory ROI. Trades at ~mid-teens next year vs speculative AI names — a value setup.
NVDA = 40 GW of US chip sales '25–30 (vs ~21 GW of DC built in the prior 25 years). GPU useful life ~7–8 years; revenue per GPU-hour ≈ the current token price (VR ~$10/h).
NVDA cutting LPDDR5 ~by half in the Vera Rubin racks — not bad news, it's a tell of how acute the scarcity is ("everything getting nerfed"). DRAM = the #1 bottleneck for AI builds, worse than CPU.

The "Kyber" rack (orthogonal backplane) slips from Rubin Ultra 2027 to ≥2028; Rubin Ultra 2027 stays on Oberon/NVL72. AI PCB/CCL impact ~5%/8% in 2027 (up to ~11%/16% in 2028). Benefits copper cables.

NVDA's HBM $17–18 → $30–32/GB (+70–80%). GPU+HBM ~$4.3M/rack; total memory bill ~$200B in 2027. Risk: if hyperscalers force HBM consignment, it compresses revenue/ASP/EPS — "the stock that looks cheap isn't that cheap".
NVDA gets the LOWEST HBM price (AMD, Broadcom, AWS pay more). HBM4 needs ~3x for ~$5/Gb in 2027. LPDDR5 = the tightest-supply product of 2027 (Vera/next-gen CPU vs smartphones).

OpenAI launches 'Jalapeño', its first custom AI chip — developed in ~9 months, fabbed with Broadcom (AVGO), aimed at LLM inference (where NVDA competes with GB300 NVL72). Signals the largest lab following GOOG-TPU / AWS-Trainium / META-MTIA in migrating inference to ASIC; if OpenAI's ≥10GW NVDA contract becomes training-only, NVDA's inference TAM there shrinks. Corroborates the 'ASIC units > merchant GPU in 2027' fragmentation thesis.

Rubin GPU ramp slower in Q2'26 on redesigns but still 2.1mn units for 2026 with a steep 2H pickup; Vera CPU units raised to 5.5mn in 2027 (from 1.6mn 2026), driving +57% NVDA CoWoS demand in 2027. Reaffirms the bullish Rubin/Vera unit trajectory into 2027.

Kyber NVL144 delayed 12+ months to 2028 (PCB midplane); NVL576 delayed/small-vol; NVL72x2 cancelled; CPO NVSwitch only at Feynman → argues there is no proven scale-up world-size path for Rubin Ultra, opening a window for AMD MI500X / Google TPUv8i 'Broadfly'. NVDA denied the delay 07-07 (see below).

China H200 re-opening: Beijing to let ByteDance/Alibaba/DeepSeek buy ~200k H200 for training — a potential re-open of the $0-in-guide China leg. First actual H200 shipments 'have begun' but 'very few' (07-14, ZTE among licensed buyers); FT reports NVDA halved its Asia buyer list and Beijing broad-sale approval is still not granted — upside real but tiny and gated, not yet in numbers.

NVDA reiterated MS semis Top Pick 'on value'. Company says Rubin Ultra ships next year (NOT 2028); the Kyber rack is replaced by a 'better solution' (a superior/larger scale-up domain), with 800V (Rubin) + CPO optical scale-out (Rubin Ultra) both on schedule — reframing the Kyber cancellation as an upgrade, not a slip. MS models NVDA GM to 73% next year (deliberately conservative vs mgmt's mid-70s).

'DC Capex Ramping to >$1.4T in 2028E' — Outperform, PT $300. Consensus AI DC capex $1.2T 2027E (+35% y/y) / >$1.4T 2028E; ~$50B/GW × cumulative 106GW 2026-30E ≈ >$5.3T (~4x 2025-26E). NVDA the primary technology enabler of the ramp — the clearest sizing of the demand pool behind the order book.

Mgmt frames NVDA at ~85% revenue share as 'a level they can sustain' — much more confident on ASICs than the market ('gives ASICs too much credit'; longest asset life vs single-purpose ASIC), and AI-lab share can RISE as NVDA ramps with the frontier lab it was shut out of. Jensen's own direct rebuttal: 'no loss of market share' — a leading frontier lab that relied heavily on internal ASICs has shifted nearly 50% of its compute to NVDA; 800V + rack-to-rack optical 'no material delay', Rubin Ultra 'on track to ship next year'.

TSM 2Q26 read-through for NVDA (still ~50%+ of TSMC's 2027 CoWoS allocation): FY26 rev guided 'slightly above 40%', FY26 capex raised to US$60-64bn, agentic-AI CPU resurgence, and demand described as strong 'all the way to 2029, 2030' with an N3-and-below supply gap 'really big' — corroborates the multi-year AI-compute demand underpinning NVDA's Blackwell+Rubin order book. Combines with the Mizuho >$1.4T-2028E DC-capex frame (07-11).

'The Paths to 25-50% GenAI ROIC' — a demand-durability read-through, NOT a rating (the note carries no NVDA rating or PT). What makes it worth logging is that MS standardises all three of its GenAI unit-economics frameworks on 1GW of NVDA GB300, i.e. the case for continued NVDA demand is now argued in the currency of NVDA's own installed base: 410,256 GB300 chips per GW; US$39bn of all-in capital cost per GW (US$23bn IT on a 5-yr life + US$16bn non-IT on a 15-yr life, ≈US$6bn/yr of depreciation) assuming ~US$4mn per GB300 rack 'consistent with our Asia semis' teams published rack BoM'; 75% utilisation; US$8.50/hr GPU rental; 2,750 tokens/sec/GPU. Outputs: hyperscaler GPU rental (IaaS) ~US$22.9bn revenue/GW at ~67% incremental EBIT margin and ~31% ROIC (23-39% across US$7.00-10.00/hr); a model-enabled API on OWNED infrastructure ~46% ROIC / ~75% incremental margin; the same API on 3P/rented infrastructure ~25% ROIC / ~31% margin. The returns math on the CURRENT generation clears a normal corporate hurdle at every layer of the stack — the cleanest available rebuttal to the 'hyperscalers can't generate FCF' bear, because it is a capital-returns calculation on hardware already deployed. MS's own caveat carried: 'while custom ASICs and prior GPU generation have lower costs, we believe chip pricing/hour and token throughput are also lower.'

Fubon's CoWoS refresh, and the number to carry is the allocation — on two DIFFERENT bases that must not be netted. NVDA's TOTAL capacity allocation reaches 1.03mn wafers in 2027 versus 629k in 2026 on a TSMC+SPIL basis (the SPIL leg supporting Vera CPU production, outside the TSMC CoWoS pool), against 945,000 wafers on a TSMC-only CoWoS basis — Figure 5 has NVDA at 51.4% (2025) → 50.1% (2026) → 50.0% (2027) of TSMC CoWoS = 346,800 → 586,500 → 945,000 wafers. Total NVDA chip output rises to 12.4mn in 2027 from 8.2mn in 2026, helped by the post-cancellation interposer math: after the four-compute-die Rubin Ultra was cancelled Fubon models '12 and 10 interposers per CoWoS wafer for Rubin and Rubin Ultra, respectively' — Rubin 12, Rubin Ultra 10 — i.e. Rubin Ultra's interposer is only marginally larger than Rubin's. Near-term the direction is the other way: Rubin's 2026 volume is cut to ~1mn on the thermal redesign and production push-out, offset by higher 3Q26 Blackwell, so the 2026 CoWoS chip-output forecast is 'largely unchanged.' Positioning stated plainly and it is the bear side: 'in the short term, we think nVidia's supply chain could potentially underperform due to Rubin's lower-than-expected volume in 2H26 and uncertain design change in the next generation rack design,' with Fubon more confident in the CPU, SPE and TPU chains.

The fullest account yet of what replaces Kyber, plus the HBM/ASP BOM. Kyber was cancelled/delayed in March/April on mid-plane bandwidth issues; it carried 576 compute dies per rack (144 GPUs × 4 compute dies) and Fubon's checks say NVDA still plans to preserve the same 576 compute dies, via one of two designs: (a) the conservative option, stay on the current Oberon rack with one system built from four racks connected by traditional scale-out (144 compute dies each, 4 × 144 = 576); or (b) a two-rack design Fubon calls 'Taycan' — each rack 144 GPUs × 2 compute dies, with NPO/CPO used for the scale-out connection BETWEEN the two racks and cable retained for scale-up inside each rack. Neither is finalised, so Fubon explicitly declines to name winners and losers ('difficult to say who will benefit and who will suffer'); the one directional call it makes is that 'we think nVidia is still aggressive in the NPO/CPO solution despite a lot of market noise.' On the BOM, a relative-advantage datapoint: HBM4 costs NVDA US$31-32/GB, up from US$17-18/GB for HBM3e in 2026, but 'for other GPU and custom-ASIC projects, we believe their HBM cost will be higher than nVidia's and may reach US$35-36 per GB, meaning the HBM cost will double in 2027' — so HBM inflation is real (~+80% for NVDA) but NVDA buys ~10-15% cheaper than the merchant/ASIC field, a scale edge that partly offsets the ASIC-TCO bear. On that BOM Fubon models the Rubin GPU price 'skyrocketing' to US$78-80K assuming NVDA holds a 75-80% chip gross margin.

events.text: GS semis bottom-up (Exhibit 3): NVDA 14/18/22 GW of AI deployments in 2026/27/28 at $50bn/GW of total capex, inside an industry build of ~20/35/57 GW (~$1.3tn 2027, ~$2.0tn 2028) — NVDA's share of GW falls from ~70% to ~39% as AVGO (5→20 GW) and MediaTek (0.4→11 GW) ramp (house arithmetic). Revenue-per-GW ladder restated from the company: Blackwell ~$25bn, Rubin ~$40bn; GS assumes ~$45bn for Feynman. Not an NVDA rating note.

events.text: Notable Capital at Jefferies' AI Summit: 'With Nvidia and AMD sold out, companies raising $100M to $1B are not even relevant enough to make the customer list'; stays bullish on NVDA 'which still trades at a discount to the market'. Jefferies: the compute imbalance could stretch beyond the 2028-29 many investors expect. Exa says AWS inference chips are 'good enough' though it still largely uses NVDA. NVDA listed BUY $225.51; no rating action.

events.text: InferenceX (AgentX 09-17 snapshot) on GLM-5.3: GB300 the lowest modelled serving cost at 150 tok/s; GB200 ~$0.044 vs $0.238 per M total tokens for AMD MI355X/ATOM at 150 tok/s (−82%), −52% at 100 and −62% at 125; $5.92 vs $28.52 per M output tokens. Caveat: GB200 p90 TTFT 14-19s vs 1.3-1.7s; with TTFT <2s, B200 $0.0666 vs MI355X $0.1265 (−47%).
